lines.text: Two islands at the southern edge of the Caribbean, rich in oil and famous for steel drums, calypso and carnival. This is Trinidad and Tobago.
In 1595 Walter Raleigh sealed his ships with tar from Pitch Lake, the largest natural lake of asphalt in the world.
Eric Williams, a historian, would lead the islands to independence as their first prime minister.
V. S. Naipaul, grandson of Indian labourers, would write A House for Mr Biswas and win the Nobel Prize.
In the 1930s people in Trinidad began beating music out of oil barrels, and the steelpan was born.
Hasely Crawford would win the country's first Olympic gold, in the hundred metres of 1976.
Kamla Persad-Bissessar would become the first woman prime minister, and return to office in 2025.
In 1962 Trinidad and Tobago became independent from Britain, a young nation built on oil and gas.
Brian Lara, a brilliant left-hander, would set the highest scores in cricket, four hundred in a Test and five hundred and one not out.
Nicki Minaj, born in Trinidad, would become one of the best-selling women in hip hop.
In 1990 armed men stormed parliament in an attempted coup, but the government held.
From pitch and oil to pan and carnival, these two islands have made a music all their own.
